alt: 空气炸锅蒜香柠檬三文鱼

summary: Salmon fillets coated with garlic and lemon zest, cooked in uncrowded batches and finished with lemon juice off the heat. For a shared table, measure doneness and plan transport and holding under applicable local authority guidance before starting.

ingredients.item: Salmon fillets, skin on, fresh or fully thawed
ingredients.quantity: 4, about 150 g each and 2.5 cm at the thickest point
ingredients.note: Fish allergen. Check thickness when estimating cooking time: a thin tail piece can cook several minutes before a centre cut of similar weight. Thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight, not on the counter, and pour the liquid away.
Grated garlic belongs in the paste and on the fish. Loose garlic in the basket scorches in the airflow and turns bitter long before the salmon is ready.

ingredients.item: Olive oil, or softened unsalted butter
ingredients.note: Butter browns faster and tastes richer. If you use it, the dish contains milk, and whatever you write on the label at the table has to say so.
Mix the zest of one into the paste before cooking. Halve the other and squeeze it over the cooked fish for fresh lemon flavour.
Optional; dill or chives are alternatives. Check every ingredient and garnish against the diners’ allergies.

method.instruction: Unwrap the salmon and check that it is fresh or fully thawed. A part-frozen fillet heats unevenly, and its outside is finished long before its middle. Pat every piece dry. The timings below assume fillets of about 2.5 cm at the thickest point; thinner tail pieces are ready sooner and want checking earlier.

Make the paste. Grate the 4 garlic cloves into the 2 tablespoons of oil or softened butter, add the zest of 1 lemon, the salt and the pepper, and stir it thick. Spread it over the flesh side of each fillet. Keep the garlic in the paste and on the fish rather than scattering it in the basket, where the airflow burns it.

Do not marinate the fish in lemon juice. Acid firms and whitens the surface without heating anything, so a fillet that has sat in juice looks further along than it is, and a long soak leaves the outside chalky. The zest goes on now; the juice waits until the fish is off the heat.

Set the air fryer to 190°C, preheating only if the manual requires it. Lay the fillets skin down in a single layer with gaps. If only 2 fit without crowding, cook the 4 fillets in separate batches; basket capacity depends on your model and fillet size.

Cook for 9 to 13 minutes as a starting point, not a guaranteed finish. Use a probe thermometer in the thickest part of each fillet, clear of the basket and metal, and reach the fish endpoint published by the applicable local food-safety authority. Confirm that endpoint before cooking; do not guess or substitute colour, flaking or time. If below it, cook for 2 more minutes and measure again. Check every batch independently.

Off the heat, squeeze over the second lemon and scatter the parsley. Between batches, use controlled hot holding under local authority guidance or promptly chill the cooked fish; a cover alone does not establish safe holding.

Before transport, check the local authority’s cold-chain or hot-holding requirements and use suitable insulated equipment with temperature monitoring. Promptly chill fish that is not being served or safely held hot. Do not assume a covered tray in a car or an insulated container alone meets those requirements.

Track preparation, waiting, transport and table time together under the applicable local authority’s transport and holding rule. Confirm its limits and discard instructions before sharing; cooling does not erase earlier exposure. If you cannot establish compliant handling, do not serve it or rely on reheating to rescue it.

yield_note: Four fillets, cooked in 2 batches in a small basket. Serves four as a main course, or six to eight as one dish on a shared table alongside others. About 35 minutes from fridge to packed container. For a larger quantity, keep the basket uncrowded and allow another cycle of 9 to 13 minutes for every extra 2 fillets. Editorial measuring convention for these original notes: tablespoon 20 mL; teaspoon 5 mL. These are volume measures, not gram conversions.

caveats: A probe thermometer is required in the thickest part of each fillet, clear of metal. Confirm and measure the applicable local authority’s fish endpoint; do not guess it or use colour, flaking or elapsed time instead.
Measure every batch, and the thickest fillet in each one. A centre cut and a thin tail piece will never be ready at the same minute.
Use fresh or fully thawed fish. Thaw frozen fillets in the fridge overnight rather than on the counter, and pour the liquid away before the paste goes on.
Do not crowd the basket. Piled-up fillets trap steam, brown poorly and heat unevenly, which can leave the centre undercooked. Cook a second batch if needed.

For sharing, follow the local authority’s transport and holding rules, monitor temperatures and track all relevant time cumulatively. An insulated container or a covered tray alone is not a verified cold chain or hot-holding system. Do not serve food whose handling cannot be confirmed.
Raw fish and its packaging contaminate surfaces. Wash hands, board and knife, and never put cooked fillets back on the plate or into the container that held them raw.

Fish is an allergen; butter adds milk. This is not an exhaustive allergen list and no ingredient, herb or garnish is guaranteed allergen-free. Check packets, sauces, cross-contact and the diners’ individual allergies; bring an ingredient list to the shared table.
These are practical notes: this project has not cooked this recipe, it has had no professional food-safety review, and it is not a substitute for the guidance published where you live.
